On Wednesday night, one person died and another was injured in a suspected terrorist attack near Hebrew University in Jerusalem. According to the Israel Police, a 37-year-old Arab man from East Jerusalem drove his car into two people who were waiting at a bus stop in the French Hill neighborhood. The police identified the man who died as 26-year-old Shalom Yohai Cherki. A 20-year-old woman is still in serious condition. The driver has been arrested and is being investigated by the General Security Services.

Lauren Bacall, a famous actress who passed away in 2014, has put her large art collection up for sale. The collection features works by some of the most important artists of the 20th century. It was sold at an auction in New York on March 31, after being shown in Hong Kong, Paris, London, and Los Angeles.

Bacall became famous in 1944 with her first movie, "To Have And Have Not." She was 89 years old when she died in August 2014. It was during the filming of "To Have And Have Not" that she met her husband, Humphrey Bogart. At the 2015 Golden Globes, actor George Clooney honored her

People in Kiev, Ukraine, are worried about who might be killing people who supported Ukraine’s former president, Viktor Yanukovych. This idea isn’t new, but it became a big concern this week after two famous people were shot and killed in the city. One was Oleg Kalashnikov, a former lawmaker who was close to Yanukovych. He was shot and died around 7 p.m. on Wednesday when he arrived at his apartment building. The other victim was a journalist who supported Russia.

Chile will soon recognize civil unions for same-sex couples. On Monday, President Michelle Bachelet signed a new law that allows these unions, joining several other South American countries. Bachelet said this is an important step toward treating gay and straight couples equally. The law will start in six months. It gives legal status to relationships between two people of the same sex, as well as to relationships between a man and a woman. The Chilean government estimates that about 2 million people will benefit from this change.

Next time you fly to Florida, look out the window. Whether you are visiting family, going to Disney World, or heading to the beach, try to sit by the window as you land. You will see the Everglades, a large swamp area. This place shows how human mistakes can cause damage and how hard it is to fix them. From the air, the swamp looks like a messy, empty area full of dangerous animals like snakes, scorpions, rats, roaches, alligators, and mosquitoes. In fact, one researcher caught 365,000 biting insects in just one trap in a single night.

In early April, ISIS militants took control of Yarmouk, a Palestinian refugee camp near Damascus that had been under siege and bombing by Syrian forces for over two years. Hundreds of masked fighters flooded into the streets, defeating several local militia groups. The residents were terrified by the violence. One resident, who asked not to be named, told CNN that ISIS killed people in the streets, including three men who were caught and executed in front of others. Now, ISIS controls almost the entire camp.

According to a study published on Friday, China’s internet censors are no longer satisfied with just using the "Great Firewall" to block citizens from reading Western news or other content they dislike. They have created a new tool called the "Great Cannon" and are using it to attack servers outside of China, including those in the United States. The study’s authors note that this tool operates openly. They suggest that by attacking other countries so obviously, China may have expected to face international criticism.

A spokesman for the prosecutor’s office in Dusseldorf, Germany, said on Monday that investigators have not found any proof of why co-pilot Andreas Lubitz crashed Germanwings Flight 9525. They found no writings or conversations where he explained his reasons or admitted to any plans. However, medical records show that Lubitz had suicidal thoughts and received psychotherapy at some point before he became a pilot.

On Sunday, the leader of Yemen’s Houthi rebels said he would not give up. This statement came after a top Saudi military official claimed that weeks of airstrikes had significantly weakened the group.

Abdul-Malik al-Houthi, the rebel leader, said in a TV speech that his fighters would not leave the main cities or government buildings. He added that anyone thinking the rebels would surrender was wrong.

These comments followed more than three weeks of bombings by a Saudi-led coalition. The coalition’s goal was to push back the Houthis, who took over the capital, Sanaa, in January and removed President Abdu Rabu Mansour Hadi from power.

On April 19, 1995, Timothy McVeigh blew up a large truck bomb outside the Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City. This attack killed 168 people, including men, women, and children, and hurt hundreds more. It is still the worst act of homegrown terrorism in U.S. history.

The media covered the event heavily, using phrases like "attack on the heartland" and "America's lost innocence." The bombing shocked the country. People were not just focused on how big the tragedy was, but on the fact that American citizens had attacked their own government with a level of violence that had never been seen before.

If you cared deeply about something, would you protest? Would you make a sign or join a demonstration? How long could you keep going when people ignored you or did nothing?

A year ago, more than 200 Nigerian girls were kidnapped from their school by Boko Haram militants. In response, millions of people around the world used social media to ask for their safe return. Charles Alasholuyi was one of them, along with celebrities and world leaders. They expressed their anger using the hashtag #BringBackOurGirls. This became one of the most popular Twitter hashtags of 2014, appearing in more than four million tweets.

However, as weeks turned into months, there was still no sign of the missing girls. Eventually, the attention on the campaign faded

Barney Frank, a retired former congressman, recently spoke to a full audience in Chicago. He talked about his 45 years of working in public service. Frank was the first member of Congress to marry someone of the same sex while holding office. He also criticized politicians who hide their sexual orientation but vote against LGBT rights. When an audience member asked about a California ballot measure that would allow killing gay people, Frank said he did not know about it. He told the young man not to worry about "crazy people."

A violent attack at Garissa University College in Kenya has killed nearly 150 people, including students, and injured dozens more. According to officials, gunmen stormed the campus early Thursday morning while people were attending morning prayers. They shot randomly and took hostages before security forces killed them. The U.S. Embassy in Nairobi stated that the militant group Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility for the attack. This tragedy happens just months after Al-Shabaab killed non-Muslim workers at a Kenyan quarry. The group has been responsible for many attacks in the region and has also recruited some Americans, especially Somali-Americans living in Minnesota.

A university in South Africa is celebrating the removal of a statue of a British colonial leader after weeks of protests. Students at the University of Cape Town used social media to demand that the statue of Cecil Rhodes be taken down, arguing that his history is marked by racism. They started a campaign last month using the hashtag #RhodesMustFall. Four weeks later, the campaign is now called #RhodesHasFallen. On Wednesday, the university announced that a heritage authority gave permission to remove the statue from the campus. The university stated that these steps are being taken to keep the statue safe while its future is being decided.

Syria is becoming increasingly terrible, and this is happening openly. According to an opposition group, the number of deaths has doubled in just one year. The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights reported on Thursday that 310,000 people have died since the civil war began. A year before that, the number was 162,402, and two years prior, the United Nations estimated 70,000 deaths. The UN says that violence has pushed more than half of Syrians into extreme poverty, leaving them in desperate need of help. Food rations are being reduced because there are not enough donations.

Ailina Tsarnaeva, the sister of Dzhokhar and Tamerlan Tsarnaev, appeared quiet and shy when she went to Manhattan Criminal Court. However, prosecutors say she was not afraid to threaten someone she saw as a rival.

According to a criminal complaint, Tsarnaeva called a woman this summer and told her, "Leave my man alone" and "Stop looking for him." She also said, "I know people that can put a bomb where you live."

Because of who Tsarnaeva is, prosecutors did not think these words were a joke. They charged her with aggravated harassment, which she denies. When she left court last December, she and her lawyer refused to talk about the case.

Police in Gaza took a door with a drawing by the British artist Banksy on Thursday after a disagreement about its sale. A police official told CNN that the door’s owner, Rabea Darduna, went to court. He said he did not know the door was valuable when he sold it for just $175. The police in Khan Younis, in southern Gaza, will keep the iron door until a court date is set. Darduna said that when his home was destroyed in last summer’s war, he felt he had lost everything, except for the doorway and the door.

On Tuesday, the Saudi-led coalition continued its attacks on Houthi rebels in Yemen. As the coalition took more control, many locals fled the area and dozens of civilians were killed.

Five days after starting airstrikes, the coalition destroyed the air defense systems of the Houthis and supporters of former President Ali Abdullah Saleh. They also made almost all air bases and runways unusable, according to a Saudi source.

Additionally, Saudi Arabia’s navy now controls all Yemeni ports. They are blocking most traffic, allowing only closely monitored non-military medical supplies to pass through.

Guus Hiddink, the manager of the Netherlands team, strongly criticized his own fans for booing Andres Iniesta during the Netherlands' 2-0 win against Spain on Tuesday. He called the fans a "disgrace."

Spain’s coach, Vicente del Bosque, used a different lineup for the match at the Amsterdam Arena. Iniesta started on the bench and came into the game in the 76th minute. When he did, the home fans booed and jeered him loudly.

The Netherlands won thanks to first-half goals from defender Stefan de Vrij and midfielder Davy Klaassen. Although the win boosted the team's morale, Hiddink was unhappy with how Iniesta was treated. The text also notes that Iniesta was seen controlling the ball during

Scotland will find out on May 21 whether its September 2016 Euro qualifier against Georgia will be played without spectators. UEFA has started disciplinary proceedings against the Georgian Football Federation because fans entered the field twice during Georgia’s 2-0 loss to Germany in Tbilisi on Sunday. UEFA will also investigate claims that home fans set off fireworks. Additionally, officials will look into several safety violations, including blocked stairs, locked gates, and staff failing to conduct body searches at the Boris Paichadze Stadium.

Football agents were left waiting on Wednesday for news about new rules. Starting April 1, the system for licensing agents will change. Now, anyone can become a football agent if they pay £500 for the first year. After that, the FA will charge £250 each year to renew the license. Agents who already had a license do not need to change anything. The FA was supposed to put a link on its website for agents to register, but as of 1 pm, the link was not yet available. Mel Stein believes these new rules will cause chaos. These changes happen because FIFA has stopped regulating agents.

Maksims Uvarenko, the Latvian goalkeeper for CSKA Sofia, has not received his salary for three months since he joined the club in January on an 18-month contract. Because of this financial trouble, he has had to ask his parents to send him money to pay his rent. Despite these money problems, Uvarenko says he is impressed by the club’s fans and their passionate support, calling them "unique." He told local media, "The lack of money is the biggest problem I've faced at CSKA."

David Moore, 25, got very angry while driving. He had just left his house and was stuck in heavy traffic next to Rafal Cegielka, 45. Mr. Cegielka was picking up his child from St John's Primary School in Burnley, Lancashire.

Moore hit Mr. Cegielka in the face. Then, he used a hockey stick to damage Mr. Cegielka’s car. This happened in front of young children. A court heard that Moore was having a bad day and lost his temper.

Spain lost 2-0 to Holland on Tuesday. This loss brought back painful memories of Spain’s bad performance in the 2014 World Cup. However, Gerard Pique says coach Vicente del Bosque should not worry too much about losing three friendlies in a row.

Holland’s 5-1 win over Spain in the 2014 World Cup had ended Spain’s six-year reign as the best team in the world. In this recent match, Holland scored two goals early in the game. They kept their lead despite strong pressure from Spain in the second half, winning 2-0 at the Amsterdam Arena.

Police say a New York City mother, Ulrike Berger, 44, has taken her seven-year-old daughter, Kaia, to Germany during a custody dispute. A court order forbids Berger from leaving the country with the child. However, police believe the pair flew from New York to Germany on March 22, one day after Kaia was dropped off for a weekend visit.

Berger and Kaia were last seen at Berger’s home in Boerum Hill, Brooklyn, at 10 a.m. on March 21, when Kaia’s father left her there. Police are now searching for them for violating the custody order.

A large fire burned through dry heathland near the south coast of Britain. The fire created big flames and thick, bad-smelling smoke. It destroyed an area the size of 100 football pitches, looking like a scene from a disaster movie. This happened after days of storms in Britain that knocked down trees and closed roads. The 70-hectare area in Dorset was very dry because it is on a hillside, so rainwater ran off the slope. Fire investigators confirmed that the fire was started on purpose. They found that three separate areas of heath were destroyed: one half-hectare, one hectare, and 70 hectares.

Last night, emergency services in Britain received 600 calls every hour as people celebrated the New Year in 2012. Paramedics were overwhelmed, and in Cambridge, a military field hospital was opened to help drunk partygoers. The London Ambulance Service said that at the busiest time, they handled more than 600 calls per hour—more than three times the usual number. In Manchester, one man collapsed on the sidewalk next to an ambulance while two other partygoers walked by eating late-night food. In another part of Manchester, a man was slumped in a doorway while two women walked past, celebrating the New Year.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet says his mental strength helped him bounce back after being dropped from the team last December. Manager Brendan Rodgers removed him "indefinitely" because of poor performance, but Mignolet returned quickly when another player, Brad Jones, hurt his thigh. The 27-year-old Belgian player explained that he stayed positive despite being upset about being cut from the squad. He told FourFourTwo, "I was positive."

On Tuesday, large hailstones, about the size of plums, fell across the Southern United States. Many people went outside to film the unusual weather. A man named Arke USA from Bryant, Arkansas, recorded video of the ice balls hitting his backyard and splashing into his swimming pool. The video shows the hailstones falling quickly and breaking when they hit the ground. Even though the temperature was around 80 degrees, the hard ice did not melt right away. Within seconds, the patio was covered in white ice pellets.

Nine people from the *Liana's Ransom*, a replica pirate ship, had to leave their vessel after it lost power in rough seas off the coast of Maine. The ship’s engines failed around 12:35 a.m. on Monday, and the sails got tangled around the mast. The Coast Guard rescued the crew using lifeboats on Tuesday. The crew members had to jump from the ship to get into the lifeboats. The Canadian charter ship was left floating about 30 miles east of Portland.

Stunning photos show blue glowing algae lighting up Australia’s east coast. The pictures were taken in Jervis Bay, on the south coast of New South Wales, showing the bright glow on one of Australia’s popular beaches. Photographer Andy Hutchinson called the sight a “beautiful supernatural scene” caused by millions of tiny sea creatures (plankton) that emit light. A similar event happened at Manly Beach in Sydney in August 2014. At that time, an oceanography expert told Daily Mail Australia that people did not need to worry about the algae.

A 17-year-old boy named Rahul Kumar was rescued by zoo security after he jumped into a lion enclosure at the Kamla Nehru Zoological Park in Ahmedabad, India. He climbed over the fence and ran toward the lions, shouting that he was going to kill them. Later, he explained that he was drunk and believed he had a good chance of winning against the animals.

A 12-year-old boy in Nanchang, China, survived after falling from a fifth-story window. He landed on a car parked below, which saved his life. His father said the boy was likely sleepwalking when he fell. The incident happened last Saturday night. A hotel receptionist across the street heard a loud crash around midnight and thought it was a car accident.

Drew Miller, a player for the Red Wings, is excited to play again just one day after getting a serious cut on his face. The injury could have blinded him, but Miller said he feels very lucky that his eye was not hurt. He spoke at practice on Wednesday while wearing a full face mask. He had a large, bloody wound that needed 50 to 60 stitches to close. Although he has a scar across his eye, reports say his eyesight is fine.

Filipe Luis says he wants to stay at Chelsea until his contract ends, even though Atletico Madrid might try to bring him back this summer. He joined Chelsea from Atletico last July with a three-year deal, but he has had trouble making the left-back position his own at the club. Atletico hopes this gives them an advantage, but Luis stated, “I am happy at Chelsea. I want to stay at the club until the end of my contract.”

Charlie Sumner, a 20-year-old fan of Reading Football Club, is facing a three-year ban from stadiums. This penalty comes after he ran onto the field topless and did four front flips during his first game at the Madejski Stadium.

The incident happened last month during an FA Cup quarter-final replay, where Reading beat Bradford City 3-0. Sumner performed his stunt while his team was already leading 3-0. He landed on his back and was then taken away by security guards.

Sumner, who described attending his first game as a "brilliant experience," now faces the potential three-year ban for this action.

A video shows a van driving fast near Salé, Morocco. About six men were sitting on the roof. The van was carrying football fans. As the van turned a corner, it swerved side to side and then tipped over. The men on the roof were thrown off. A car following the van recorded the scary moment.

England has been placed in Group D of the UEFA Under-17 European Championships, along with the Republic of Ireland, Holland, and Italy. The tournament will take place in Bulgaria in May.

England’s team, managed by John Peacock, is the current champion. They won last year’s final in Malta by defeating Holland on penalties. To move on to the quarter-finals of this year’s tournament, England must beat Holland again. This year’s competition is larger than before, expanding from eight teams to 16 for the first time.

In a separate event, Danny Collinge scored England’s first goal against Norway during the qualifying rounds and ran away to celebrate.

An elephant in South Africa’s Kruger National Park was relaxing by a small pool with its family when a male buffalo came too close. Annoyed, the elephant tried to spray water from its trunk to make the buffalo leave. It missed its target. The baby elephant stayed close to its parent for protection while the buffalo drank from the pool.

Michael Thorpe, a former pub owner, has won an eight-year legal battle to clear his name. He was originally convicted in November 2006 for showing Premier League football matches on foreign TV channels at his pub, the Stoke Inn in Plymouth, Devon, without permission from official broadcasters. The court has now overturned his conviction. However, Thorpe, 55, says the long fight cost him heavily, including the loss of his pub.

The Irish Football Association hopes that structural damage at Windsor Park, their stadium in Belfast, will not stop them from hosting a key Euro 2016 match against Romania in June. Cracks were found in the West Stand on Tuesday morning, so the area was closed off while engineers checked the damage. A spokesperson said the association learned overnight that the West Stand had been damaged. This damage occurred on Monday night.

Charlie Sumner, 20, has been banned from football for three years. The ban happened after he ran onto the field topless and did four front flips during his first game at the stadium.

The incident took place last month at Reading's Madejski Stadium during an FA Cup match against Bradford City. At the time, Reading was winning 3-0. Sumner landed on his back after each flip before security guards tackled him.

A BMW driver who had five children in the car was arrested today. This happened after a talented student, Hina Shamim, was hit by the car and killed while walking to the library.

Hina, 21, died near the University of Kingston in London last night. She was just weeks away from turning 22.

Friends have left flowers at the scene. They said Hina, who was originally from Peterborough and went by the nickname "Hyena," was very much loved and a charming, lovely girl. She was killed while walking a short distance from her home to the library.

A mother and her teenage daughter were arrested after a video of them fighting with a high school student went online. The incident happened on Tuesday at Langham Creek High School in Houston. According to Channel 2, the mother was angry because the student had allegedly been bullying her own daughter. The video shows the mother, who has not been named, wearing a black top on the right, and the other student, who is the victim, wearing white in the center.

Stoke City’s boss, Tony Scholes, hopes to keep Asmir Begovic, the team’s goalkeeper, as his contract ends next year. Begovic, who plays for the Bosnia national team, has often been linked with other clubs while playing at the Britannia Stadium. Even though he has just over 12 months left on his current deal, Scholes believes they can meet the 27-year-old’s goals.

Scholes told The Sentinel: “Clearly, Asmir is a great goalkeeper, and we really want him to stay at the club. I think it’s normal for people to talk about what happens next when you have really good players.”

A bus driver in Auckland, New Zealand, was caught reading a newspaper while driving. A passenger filmed the incident and sent the video to the bus company, Ritchies Coachlines, along with a complaint. The video shows the driver turning the pages of the newspaper while the bus is moving. When the bus stops at traffic lights, the driver looks closely at one of the pages. The boss of Ritchies Coachlines, Andrew Ritchie, said he was embarrassed by the driver’s actions and called him a "complete idiot."

West Ham manager Sam Allardyce says that defender Winston Reid will be ready to play in Saturday’s game against Leicester City. However, Enner Valencia will not be available.

Reid had been injured since March 4, when West Ham lost 1-0 to Chelsea. He hurt his hamstring during that match. But during the break for international games, he returned to full training.

Valencia missed West Ham’s last two games against Arsenal and Sunderland because of an unusual toe injury he suffered in mid-March. Allardyce says Valencia is still not ready to play.

Allardyce confirmed, “We’ve got Winston back in full training.”

Five days before his wedding to his college sweetheart, Brittany Huber, last May, John Redman was in a terrible car crash on a Georgia highway. The accident killed Brittany and left John with severe injuries. Doctors said he would likely spend the rest of his life in a nursing home and use a wheelchair.

John was 25 and worked as an assistant basketball coach at Dalton State College. Despite these difficult odds, he made a surprising recovery. On March 24, he helped his team win a championship title.

Lucas (on the left) and Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard played in a charity game at Anfield on Sunday. Lucas, a Brazilian midfielder, wants to get back to his best form after recovering from an injury.

From late November until February, he started 16 out of 19 games. During this time, the team’s results improved significantly. However, he hurt his groin in a match against Everton in February and missed 10 games.

He did not play in the loss to Manchester United, which was Liverpool’s first league defeat since mid-December. But he played the full 90 minutes in Sunday’s charity game at Anfield.

Are you tired of boring father-daughter photos? Japanese photographer Yûki Aoyama has found a fun way to fix this. In his new book, *Daughter and Salary Man*, he shows teenagers standing still next to their fathers who are jumping in the air. In every picture, the daughter looks at the camera with a straight face, while her father strikes a dramatic pose.

Police are looking for a man aged between 50 and 60 who robbed a bank in Fairwater, Cardiff, at 12:30 pm. He took £3,000 in cash and fled the scene. The robbery happened at a Lloyds Bank branch.

Police have released CCTV images of the suspect. He is a white male, between 5ft 9in and 6ft tall, with greying black hair and glasses. He was wearing black clothes. No one was hurt during the robbery. Police are confident that members of the public can help identify him.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has removed Morocco’s ban from the next two African Cup of Nations tournaments. Previously, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) had kicked Morocco out of the 2017 and 2019 events and fined them $1 million. The CAF also asked for an additional $9 million in compensation because Morocco withdrew as hosts due to fears about the Ebola epidemic. The tournament was eventually won by Ivory Coast, who hosted it in Equatorial Guinea. Now, Morocco is allowed to take part in the next two editions of the competition.

Tom Boyd thinks Jason Denayer’s time on loan at Celtic has been so successful that he is now ready to try for a spot at Manchester City next season. This would mean Celtic manager Ronny Deila’s goal of keeping the young Belgian player for another year would fail. However, Boyd also sees a good side to this. He believes Denayer’s success can serve as a great example to encourage other young players to choose Celtic for their next career step. The 19-year-old defender has done well during his loan at Celtic this season. He also recently earned his first international game for Belgium in a Euro 2016 match against Cyprus.

Andros Townsend proved his critics wrong with a great goal for England. He said that people who doubted him, like Paul Merson, actually helped motivate him in Italy.

This has been a confusing season for the 23-year-old, who has not played as well as he did when he first started playing for the national team. However, England manager Roy Hodgson still believed in him. Townsend showed his thanks with an amazing goal at Juventus Stadium.

He scored England’s equalizing goal in a 1-1 friendly match against Italy in Turin on Tuesday night. After scoring, Townsend celebrated with his Tottenham teammates, Ryan Mason and Kyle Walker.

Chinese company Dalian Wanda Group has officially bought a 20% stake in Spanish soccer team Atletico Madrid. On Tuesday, at a special meeting, Wanda’s legal team approved the purchase of 726,707 shares for €45 million (£32.8 million). The deal was first announced in January, but two special meetings were required to finalize it. Wanda’s chairman, Wang Jianlin, hopes to expand Atletico Madrid’s brand in Asia. Meanwhile, Atletico Madrid’s manager, Diego Simeone, has been speaking to the media.

Antonio Conte said he had happy memories when he returned to Turin for Italy’s 1-1 tie with England. This was true even though reports said he received death threats in the days before the friendly match.

Conte became the manager of the Italian national team in August, replacing Cesare Prandelli. This happened after Italy was eliminated in the group stage of last summer’s World Cup. However, his first seven months as coach have been very difficult and unstable.

Recently, Italy had to score a late goal by Eder to tie 2-2 with Bulgaria. Also, Conte reportedly received death threats from Juventus fans after their player, Claudio Marchisio, injured his knee just before a Euro 2016 qualifying match.

Ian Murray thinks that the final month of the Scottish Championship season could help Hibernian (Hibs) finish in second place, ahead of Rangers. His team, Dumbarton, has already played both of his former clubs, Rangers and Hibs, this season, and will play them again in the coming weeks.

Even though Rangers currently have the momentum—having beaten Hibs and Cowdenbeath, while Hibs lost to Raith Rovers—Murray does not believe Rangers can keep up their current speed for the rest of the season. He expects the advantage to shift back to Hibs soon.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet posted photos of himself sitting in an airplane cockpit with pilots on his Facebook page. He took these pictures as he flew back to England after playing for Belgium in Euro 2016 qualifying matches against Cyprus and Israel.

Even though Mignolet was named in the team for both games, he did not play. Belgium’s coach, Marc Wilmots, chose Chelsea goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois instead. As a result, Mignolet did not earn any new international caps, keeping his total at 14.

Chyknell Hall Estate is for sale for £6 million. It is a large rural property near Bridgnorth, Shropshire, covering 200 acres. The estate includes a Grade II-listed manor house, five cottages, a swimming pool, a tennis court, stables, and a cricket green. The main house, Chyknell Hall, was built in 1814 and has 11 bedrooms. It has only been sold twice since it was built. Because the grounds are private and secluded, the home could appeal to famous buyers.

Two college police officers in Dallas have been put on leave without pay after a video showed them harassing four students and arresting one of them. The video shows that the officers hit the student before arresting him.

The incident happened last Wednesday at El Centro College in downtown Dallas. A student named Charles Adams recorded the event on his phone. He was smoking a cigarette nearby when he saw the officers approach the group. The students were waiting for a bus when the officers came up to them.

Gary Locke has been named the permanent manager of Kilmarnock after signing a three-year contract. He originally joined the club last summer as assistant manager to Allan Johnston. However, when Johnston left in early February, Locke took over as head coach. Since then, he has won six out of seven games. The 39-year-old will speak to the press on Friday morning. He recently shook hands with chairman Jim Mann to finalize his new deal.

This weekend, Germany’s biggest football match, known as "Der Klassiker," is taking place. The excitement is a bit lower than usual because Borussia Dortmund and Bayern Munich have dominated the league for the last five years, with Bayern Munich continuing to lead this season.

Even though the two teams are far apart in the standings—separated by 31 points and nine places—the game is still very important. The image shows Jurgen Klopp, the manager of Borussia Dortmund, celebrating with his players after they won against Hannover.

A 14-year-old schoolgirl named Deva Joseph was stuck at London Stansted airport because easyJet did not let her on her flight to Spain. The airline said she had too much hand luggage—two bags instead of one. Deva cried because she couldn’t go home. She offered to pay extra to put the second bag in the cargo hold, but the staff said she could only pay with a credit card. Since Deva is too young to have a credit card, she couldn’t pay, and she was left stranded.

Gordon Robson, 26, killed John Potts, 45, with one punch to the back of the head. The hit was so strong that it made a loud cracking sound.

Robson was drunk after attending his grandfather’s funeral. He punched Potts, a father, after Potts tried to stop a fight outside the NE38 Sports Bar in Washington, Tyne and Wear. This happened in November last year.

Robson has a history of violent crimes. He was sentenced to three and a half years in prison.

Scoring against your old team and making a perfect set-piece happen are two of the best feelings in football. For Notts County player Ellen White, Thursday night was special because she did both at once against Arsenal in the Women's Super League.

In the 26th minute, Notts County got a free kick near the penalty box. Laura Bassett and Alex Greenwood seemed to mess up the play, with Bassett almost running into Greenwood. This caused confusion. But Ellen White spun around near the box and kicked the ball into the corner, scoring against her former club.

High school girls in China are practicing military-style knife drills. As they perform eight specific movements, they shout commands like "kill, stab, slash, and jab." The students from Huizhou Integrated High School’s Class 27 are being trained by Inspector Tan, a former special forces soldier. The 68 girls, who are between 16 and 18 years old, use fake knives for safety. School official Huang Anruo confirmed that the daggers are not real.

We spend one-third of our lives sleeping, but many people ignore what their bodies and minds need to feel rested. A study by the Sleep Health Foundation shows that 30% of Australians complain about not getting enough sleep every day. Professor David Hillman says that if you miss sleep, you have to make up for it to stay functional throughout the week. On average, adults need about eight hours of sleep each night, with a healthy range of seven to nine hours.

Video has been posted online showing a fight between neighbors in a Perth suburb. The video, which was uploaded to Facebook today, shows an angry woman shouting racist insults at a group of men who appear to be of African descent. She is speaking to them from over her fence.

The woman then goes into her neighbor’s front yard holding a metal crowbar. She yells at the men and swings the crowbar at them. The men then grab their own weapons, and a physical fight breaks out.

In the video, the woman says, “I don’t deal with monkeys, go on now you f*****g monkeys.”

Manchester City, Arsenal, and Chelsea are all trying to sign 19-year-old Valencia defender Jose Luis Gaya this summer, hoping to take him away from Real Madrid. Sportsmail’s Pete Jenson looks at why these English clubs are so interested in the Spanish Under-21 player.

The main reason is money. Gaya’s release clause is only £13.5 million. This is very cheap compared to Luke Shaw, who was about the same age and had similar potential but cost £27 million. It would be foolish not to look at him, even though some people worry he might not be good enough for the Premier League. The text also notes a photo of Gaya playing for Valencia against Sevilla earlier this season.

Police in Oregon are asking the public for help to identify a motorcyclist who saved two teenagers. A 59-year-old man named Edward West allegedly pointed a gun at the teens in Salem and told them, "get ready to die." Just then, a stranger on a green motorcycle rode up and used his helmet to knock the gun out of West’s hands. This allowed the teenagers to escape.

Tim Sherwood has told Aston Villa captain Ron Vlaar that he needs to prove himself again as he gets ready to return to the team. Sherwood wants the healthy defender to help the struggling club finish the season strongly. He also warned Vlaar that people might have forgotten his great performance at the World Cup last year.

Vlaar played a key role in helping the Netherlands reach the semi-finals in Brazil, even though he missed a penalty in the shootout against Argentina. His performance there led to rumors that Manchester United might sign him. Now, the strong Dutch defender is returning from injury to help Aston Villa fight against being relegated. He will be back in action when the team plays at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Tim Sherwood says he is not worried about Aston Villa being sold this summer. He wants to build a team that fits his style for next season, as long as the club avoids being relegated.

It is reported that the current owner, Randy Lerner, is talking in detail with a potential buyer. If someone else buys the club, people might wonder if Sherwood will keep his job. However, Sherwood is focused only on keeping the team in the league. After that, he plans to use the summer break to make long-term changes.

In short, the manager says he is not concerned about the takeover talks. This comes after Christian Benteke scored in a big win against Sunderland last month.

It is well known that Celtic wants Manchester City to let Jason Denayer return to Parkhead on loan next season. However, getting what you want is not always easy, and City’s recent statements suggest this might not happen. Manchester City manager Manuel Pellegrini said that his young academy players are not yet ready to play for the first team. Because of this, players like Denayer may have to come back from their loans to help fill the squad. Denayer has done a good job while playing for Celtic on loan this season.

Southampton manager Ronald Koeman is waiting to know exactly when Fraser Forster will return from knee surgery before deciding if the team needs to sign another goalkeeper this summer. Forster was injured two weeks ago during a 2-0 win against Burnley. Doctors say he could be back in four to twelve months. Koeman does not want to give a specific date for his return. He believes current backup Kelvin Davis is good enough for now, but admits he might need to find another goalkeeper if Forster’s recovery takes too long.

Steve Evans, the manager of Rotherham, was very angry after his team lost a close match against Birmingham. Rotherham was in danger of being relegated from the league.

Birmingham took the lead in the first half with goals from Robert Tesche and Clayton Donaldson. Matt Derbyshire then scored for Rotherham, making the score closer.

About an hour into the game, Birmingham player Rob Kiernan handled the ball clumsily while near Derbyshire. Derbyshire fell down in the penalty area, and Rotherham asked the referee, Dean Whitestone, to award them a penalty kick. The referee refused. Evans was visibly upset, but Birmingham kept their lead and won the game. Robert Tesche was shown celebrating after scoring Birmingham's first goal.

Virgil van Dijk’s frustration is clear. The Netherlands team has already let in more goals in five Euro 2016 qualifying matches than they did in their entire World Cup qualifying campaign. Despite this, national team coach Guus Hiddink has not contacted him. Van Dijk was selected for two squads last year, but his progress was short-lived. When the Netherlands drew 1-1 with Turkey recently, Van Dijk was on vacation in the Arabian Gulf, spending time with his club teammates at Celtic. Even though he has been playing very well for Celtic, he was not called up to the national team.

Celtic are angry with the Scottish Football Association (SFA) about the ticket prices for their Scottish Cup semi-final against Inverness, which will take place later this month at Hampden.

The match has already caused problems for Inverness fans because it is scheduled for 12:15 pm on Sunday, April 18. This time is too early, as the first trains from Inverness do not arrive in Glasgow until after the game starts.

Celtic has now complained about the cost of tickets. Tickets for the North and South stands cost £23, while tickets for the East Stand are £15 for adults and £5 for concessions.

Paul Murray, the interim chairman of Rangers, said on Thursday night that the previous management teams are entirely responsible for the club being removed from the stock exchange. The club, based at Ibrox, must be delisted from the Alternative Investment Market (AIM) because it could not find a new nominated advisor (Nomad) to meet the required regulations. However, Murray insists that the new board’s future plans remain unchanged and that planned investments will still happen.

Wayne Rooney and his England teammates were unhappy with how poorly they started their match against Italy on Tuesday night. This game was a friendly at Juventus Stadium, taking place nine months after the two teams met at the World Cup. Even though England had won their previous seven games in a row, they struggled during the first half. As a result, they deservedly lost the first half after Italy’s Graziano Pelle scored with a header. The match ended in a 1-1 draw. Afterward, England captain Wayne Rooney said that he and the other players were upset by their performance in the first half.

Dundee United’s board has responded to strong criticism from two major supporters' groups, Arabtrust and the Federation of Dundee United Supporters Clubs. These groups are shocked to learn that 25% of the £6.3 million paid for players Ryan Gauld, Andrew Robertson, Stuart Armstrong, and Gary Mackay-Steven went as commissions to unnamed people. The supporters also questioned how much money chairman Stephen Thompson actually invested in the club. In response, the board defended their work by pointing to the team’s success on the field.

Gary Locke will officially become the permanent manager of Kilmarnock on Friday. This happens exactly eight weeks after he was first asked to manage the team until the end of the season. The club will make the announcement on Friday morning, and Locke will sign a three-year contract. The 39-year-old, who previously managed Hearts, thanked the players on Thursday for their hard work. Their efforts helped him gain the support of the new chairman, Jim Mann, since he took over as caretaker manager in February, replacing Allan Johnston.

Chinese parents are very focused on raising children who are exceptionally talented, whether they are ten-year-olds entering university or four-year-olds who can dance like Michael Jackson. Now, a new basketball star is becoming famous. A video has gone viral in China, showing a young boy with amazing basketball skills that are better than many professional players. The boy, named Mai Zizhuo, is five years old. According to People's Daily Online, he has been playing basketball since he was two and a half. The video shows him making many baskets and then dribbling two basketballs at the same time while running.

Bayern Munich will miss versatile left-back David Alaba for the end of the season because he has a torn knee ligament and will be out for about seven weeks. Alaba was already out for three months earlier this year due to a partial tear in his right knee. He got injured while playing for Austria in a 1-1 tie against Bosnia on Tuesday. The 22-year-old told the club’s website, “I am bitterly disappointed,” but added that his big goal is to be ready for the final game of the season. The injury happened when Emir Spahic tackled Alaba during Austria’s match against Bosnia-Herzegovina.

Hull KR have signed experienced Australian player Dane Tilse from the Canberra Raiders to replace Michael Weyman and Ryan Bailey, who are no longer with the team. Tilse, 30, is 6ft 7in and weighs over 17 stone. He has signed a two-and-a-half-year deal with Hull KR (the Robins) and will join them as soon as the paperwork is finished and the Raiders release him. Tilse has played 200 games in Australia. He will work with his former teammate Terry Campese, who is now Hull KR’s captain and recently signed a two-year contract extension. Tilse is a direct replacement for Weyman, who retired last month because of an injury.

Livingston manager Mark Burchill believes that midfielder Darren Cole wants to play in Sunday’s Petrofac Cup final, even though the match takes place just one week after the tragic death of his cousin.

Darren Cole’s cousin, 22-year-old Shaun Cole, was found dead on a street in Miami last weekend. He is believed to have been hit by a car in a hit-and-run accident. Shaun was a soldier who had served in Afghanistan. He was on holiday in Florida while on leave and had attended a music festival before being found on the sidewalk with a head injury that turned out to be fatal.

Despite this loss, Mark Burchill is hopeful that Darren Cole will play for Livingston on Sunday.

Alan Smith has denied claims that Liverpool fans attacked the ambulance carrying him to the hospital after he was seriously injured. This happened nine years ago, during Manchester United’s 1-0 FA Cup loss to Liverpool.

Smith broke his leg and dislocated his ankle in February 2006 while trying to block a free-kick by John Arne Riise. At the time, reports said Liverpool fans tried to stop his trip to the hospital by throwing bottles, beer glasses, and stones at the ambulance, and even shaking the vehicle.

Ronny Deila has confirmed that Celtic is interested in signing Hearts captain Danny Wilson this summer. According to Sportsmail, Celtic is considering making an offer of £400,000 for the defender, who has previously played for Rangers and Liverpool. Wilson has one year left on his current contract. However, Hearts owner Ann Budge says the club has no need to sell him, even though he will be out of contract at the end of the season.

Ronny Deila says Celtic will not risk their chances in the Champions League by taking on another difficult pre-season travel schedule. He blames last summer’s profitable tour of the United States, Austria, and Germany for a damaging 4-1 loss to Legia Warsaw during the qualifying rounds. Celtic has earned large fees for pre-season matches and has also traveled to Australia and the Far East in recent years. Ronny Deila and Nir Bitton walked off the field after losing to Legia Warsaw. A trip to America this July has not been ruled out yet.

Franck Ribery has denied rumors that Bayern Munich wants to sign Kevin de Bruyne from Wolfsburg to replace him or his teammate Arjen Robben.

De Bruyne played mostly on loan at Chelsea for two years before joining Wolfsburg, which is currently second in the league. This season, he has scored nine goals and leads the league in assists with 16, which is seven more than the next best player.

However, Ribery says that even though De Bruyne is playing well, he is not the right type of player for Pep Guardiola. Ribery believes De Bruyne has different strengths than he and Robben do.

Kelsi Langley, the girlfriend of an Arizona State University (ASU) football player, has taken back her claim that he abused her. She now says she lied because of her mood swings.

Her boyfriend, Davon Durant, is a talented linebacker who transferred to ASU from a college in Kansas. He was arrested on March 7 for domestic violence after Langley said he hit her in the face and grabbed her neck during an argument in his car.

Because of the arrest, Durant has been suspended from the football team for an unknown amount of time and might be kicked out of the university.

It is even more exciting to meet your hero at a Starbucks while wearing a shirt with their name on it, especially if they post a picture of you on their Instagram. A young boy was lucky enough to meet Justin Verlander, a pitcher for the Detroit Tigers, in this special way. Verlander took a selfie with the boy, who was wearing a dark blue shirt with Verlander’s name and jersey number, 35, on the back. You can watch a video of the moment by scrolling down.

Eden Hazard said that playing so many games for Chelsea might have made him too tired to play his best. This happened after he was taken out of the game just 62 minutes into Belgium’s win over Israel on Tuesday. Hazard has played 48 games this season for his club and his country, missing only five matches for Chelsea while helping them win the Premier League title. However, during Belgium’s difficult 1-0 victory over Israel in the European Championship qualifying, manager Marc Wilmots took him off with 28 minutes left because Hazard was having trouble beating his opponent, Orel Dgani.

Police in the Northern Territory found 20 grams of marijuana hidden inside a leg of lamb. The officers noticed a strange smell, so they used an X-ray machine to check the meat. The X-ray showed the hidden drugs. The lamb was being shipped to a company at Darwin Airport and was likely going to be sent to the Tiwi Islands, which are 100 kilometers north.

Former Premier League footballer Clarke Carlisle says he has separated from his wife, Gemma. They were married for 14 years and lived in Yorkshire. Carlisle moved out of their home as he continues to deal with depression after a suicide attempt in December. This attempt happened two days after he was arrested for suspected drunk driving.

Paul Merson, a famous former Arsenal player, had to admit he was wrong when he criticized Andros Townsend for being called up to the England team. On Tuesday night, Townsend played for Tottenham and came off the bench to score a great goal that tied the game 1-1 against Italy in Turin. This was a perfect response to Merson, who had written in a Sky Sports article that if Townsend could make the England squad, then anyone could. After scoring, Townsend celebrated with his teammates Ryan Mason and Kyle Walker.

It is common for Chelsea midfielder Cesc Fabregas to play poorly in the second half of the season. He was one of the worst players in his team’s 2-0 loss to Holland on Tuesday. The 27-year-old said he was happy to live in southwest London earlier this week, but his performance has dropped significantly. At Christmas, he looked like he would break the Premier League record for assists.

West Midlands Police arrested six people in Dover this morning on suspicion of terrorism related to Syria. The arrests happened around 8 am in the departure area of the port.

Five men and one woman were taken into custody. Four of the men are in their 20s and live in Birmingham, West Midlands. The other two suspects are a 26-year-old man and a 23-year-old woman who do not have a fixed address. All six people are currently being questioned at a police station in the West Midlands.

Today at 12:52 pm, people are most likely to buy themselves a treat. A study by VoucherCodes.co.uk found that people in Britain spend an average of £62 a week on rewards for themselves. This spending is highest at lunchtime. These treats can be small, like a bar of chocolate or a glass of wine, or expensive, like designer clothes and shoes. Surprisingly, men spend one-third more per month than women on treating themselves.

Arsene Wenger is highly respected and clearly very smart. Because of this, people often agree with what he says, even when his arguments are weak. Usually, he talks about how Arsenal’s defense is actually statistically strong, especially after their recent poor performance. Last week, however, he discussed quotas. Specifically, he addressed FA chairman Greg Dyke’s proposal to increase the number of homegrown players in a 25-player Premier League squad from eight to 12.

Charlie Austin says that his close friend Joey Barton ignored him on his first day at Queens Park Rangers, but Barton soon realized his mistake. The two became good friends after that. Austin has had a memorable first season in the Premier League, scoring 15 goals, which has led people to suggest he might play for England in the future. Although everyone knows about his close friendship with club captain Barton, their first meeting was something Austin will never forget.

This dog is definitely his owner’s best friend because he saved the man’s life. The black dog was filmed bringing a rescue rope to his owner at the Clarence J. Brown Dam and Reservoir in Springfield, Ohio, on Saturday afternoon. The video shows firefighters pulling the man to shore after he had been in water that was near freezing (zero degrees Celsius) for almost two hours. The man apparently got stuck waist-deep in mud while trying to pick up some duck hunting gear. Fortunately, he had a cell phone and was able to call 911. However, firefighters could not send a boat to help him because the river was too shallow.

Juventus coach Massimiliano Allegri admits that the fans will not fully support him until he wins them a championship. He joined the team last summer, a few months after being fired by AC Milan. Since then, he has done a great job, leading Juventus to a strong position in the race for the Serie A title. He replaced Antonio Conte last summer. On Saturday, Juventus will play Empoli at home, hoping to win three more points. Allegri is currently managing the team from the sidelines, and they are at the top of the league.

Nathan Redmond made a key play just six minutes into the game. Steven Whittaker passed the ball to him along the right sideline. Redmond ran faster than Joe Bennett and sent a low cross into the box. Bradley Johnson scored the winning goal in the second half at the Amex Stadium.

For six years, the people of Celoron, New York, have been upset by a statue of their famous hometown resident, Lucille Ball. In 2009, the town unveiled the statue, but its face looks very different from what people remember. Locals are shocked and angry because the statue looks so bad. A Facebook page called "We Love Lucy! Get Rid of this Statue" has gained more than 600 likes. The statue shows a scene from her TV show "I Love Lucy," where she is drunk and selling a health drink.

Isaac Luke, a player for the South Sydney team, is facing accusations of being homophobic. This happened after he posted an offensive comment on social media. He did this in response to insults from fans of the Canterbury Bulldogs.

On Saturday, the 27-year-old made a sincere request on his official Instagram account. He was trying to find a young South Sydney fan who was allegedly attacked at ANZ Stadium in Sydney. Luke wanted to give the boy a jersey as a gift before the Easter holiday. He hoped this gesture would help make up for the incident that left the boy in the hospital after the controversial game.

If you are afraid of spiders, this story might scare you. A man in Wangaratta, in northeast Victoria, had a scary experience. He was getting into his black Holden Ute when a large huntsman spider came out from inside the door handle.

The video shows the man spraying insect repellent on his car door. This made the spider come out from under the handle. The man told the spider to leave, saying, “Get out, you bast***.” At first, he seemed calm, but when the hairy spider’s legs came out, he yelled and jumped back in fear.

Tottenham manager Mauricio Pochettino has compared Harry Kane to Gabriel Batistuta. He also said he will support Kane when things do not go well.

Kane scored on his first game for the England national team, just 79 seconds after coming on as a substitute against Lithuania at Wembley on Friday night. This goal put him within two goals of scoring 30 times in the season.

England manager Roy Hodgson wants to keep expectations for Kane realistic. Kane has risen quickly in his career after finally joining Tottenham’s main team, following previous loans to Leicester and Norwich.

A court heard that a former footballer, who ran a £30 million investment scheme and lived like a millionaire, is now surviving on handouts. Michael McIndoe, who played for Bristol City and Wolverhampton Wanderers, convinced other footballers to join the scheme by promising a 20% return. However, the scheme failed due to heavy debts, and McIndoe was declared bankrupt last October with over £2 million in debt. Known as "Mr Big" in Marbella, where he partied with glamorous women, he is now being pursued by creditors through the courts.

Pavel Nedved, a director at Juventus, said that Barcelona wants to sign Paul Pogba. In an interview, Nedved stated that Pogba will not be leaving Juventus. He also mentioned that he was happy Juventus did not play against Barcelona in the Champions League quarter-finals.

Police say that 48-year-old James Oliver was hit by a car driven by his girlfriend, 53-year-old Linda Currier. The incident happened in Noblesboro, Maine, on Saturday night.

According to reports, Currier caught Oliver trying to sexually assault a 12-year-old girl. After they argued inside the house, she allegedly drove the car over him. Oliver suffered a serious leg injury.

Liverpool wants to sign Neto, but they face strong competition from Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) and several Spanish clubs. This is according to Neto’s agent, Stefano Castagna. Brendan Rodgers, the manager of Liverpool, is trying hard to sign the 25-year-old goalkeeper, who currently plays for Fiorentina.

Neto’s contract with Fiorentina ends in June. Earlier this season, Liverpool was interested in signing him because their regular goalkeeper, Simon Mignolet, was not playing well. Although Liverpool tried to sign Neto in January, that deal did not happen. However, it is very likely that Neto will leave Fiorentina in the summer. The paragraph also mentions a photo of Neto rushing out of his goal during a match against Roma in March, while Juan Iturbe was attacking.

A video on YouTube by Richard Stewart shows a Porsche Cayman crashing after speeding away from a green light in Prince Edward Island, Canada. The car swerves out of control, hits a concrete barrier, and loses a wheel before stopping. Stewart wrote that owning an expensive car does not make someone a good driver, and he warned people not to let their children drive their Porsches.

Before this weekend’s Premier League games, Sportsmail will give you everything you need to know about each match, including team updates, possible lineups, betting odds, and statistics from Opta. Here is the information for Sunderland’s home game against Newcastle at the Stadium of Light.

**Team News: Sunderland**

Sunderland midfielder Lee Cattermole will start the game against Newcastle on Sunday. Head coach Dick Advocaat confirmed that Cattermole is back after missing two games because he received his 10th booking of the season.

If Rory McIlroy wins the upcoming Masters, he will complete a career grand slam. This would finish a lifelong journey for the world’s top golfer. With his sponsor Bose, McIlroy released a video showing his path from playing on small greens as a child to becoming a golf star, including some difficult times. The video starts with McIlroy jogging early in the morning, with the words "Six weeks to Georgia" on the screen. It also includes an interview with McIlroy when he was young, before he became famous.

Sergio Garcia says he is focused on winning his first PGA Tour title since 2012 at this week’s Shell Houston Open, even though the Masters tournament is coming up soon. For weeks, the main topics have been Rory McIlroy’s attempt to win three major titles in a row to complete his career grand slam, and whether Tiger Woods will end his break from the game. Although the Golf Club of Houston is set up to mimic some of the conditions at Augusta, Garcia is concentrating on ending his long wait for a victory. The image shows Sergio Garcia lining up a putt during the Cadillac Championship in Doral, Florida, last month.

Riki Hughes, a 31-year-old Iraq war veteran, has been sentenced to 16 months in prison. He stole £17,000 from the Tidworth Town Football Club, where he volunteered as the club secretary.

Hughes tricked the club by claiming he was paying rent to the landlord, even though the team was using the property for free. Instead of paying the rent, he kept the money for himself. He used the funds to buy camping gear and to pay for a bachelor party trip to Las Vegas. The theft was revealed at Salisbury Crown Court.

Winning is a normal routine for Johnny Sexton. He adds major achievements to his record every year, and he is determined to keep doing so. As he got ready for a European Champions Cup quarter-final match against Saracens in Paris, the Racing Metro player and Irish star thought about his success. He said, “I have been very lucky to play for great teams with Leinster and Ireland. There have not been many years when I did not help a team win trophies.” In fact, since he became a senior player in 2010, that is the only year he did not win significant awards.

Mustafa Kamal stepped down as president of the International Cricket Council (ICC) on Wednesday. He accused India of using its power within the ICC to influence the result of the quarter-final match between Bangladesh and India.

Speaking at the airport after returning from the tournament in Australia, Kamal, who is from Bangladesh, said, "Everyone saw what happened during the Bangladesh-India match... India has influenced the outcome of the match using its position (in the ICC)."

He added, "From now on, I am a former president of the ICC. I would have reacted similarly had it happened to any other country." Kamal, who is pictured with the Cricket World Cup trophy, has now left his role as ICC President.

West Ham manager Sam Allardyce supports Nigel Pearson, the manager of Leicester City, and respects him for being independent. Allardyce worked with Pearson at Newcastle United in 2007, and the two will meet again when West Ham plays Leicester at the King Power Stadium on Saturday. This season, Pearson has been involved in several controversial incidents, such as grabbing Crystal Palace player James McArthur by the throat and getting angry with a reporter during a press conference.

Sunderland captain John O'Shea says his team must control their own destiny by beating Newcastle United for the fifth time in a row. The two teams play at the Stadium of Light on Sunday. Sunderland has won the last four games between them, but they really need these three points to stay safe in the Premier League. If Burnley beats Tottenham in the earlier game, Sunderland could drop into the relegation zone, making a win absolutely necessary.

Stoke City manager Mark Hughes is sure his team needs to stop losing to Chelsea at Stamford Bridge. Since Stoke was promoted to the Premier League in 2008, they have played Chelsea away eight times in all competitions and lost every single time.

Stoke’s last win at Chelsea’s stadium was in 1995, when they won a League Cup match. Since a 1-1 tie in 1984, Stoke has not earned even a single point in games at Chelsea’s home ground.

Mark Hughes says his team must end this losing streak. In their most recent visit, Chelsea beat Stoke 3-0, with Frank Lampard celebrating the victory.

Newcastle wants to avoid losing their third game in a row when they play their rivals, Sunderland, this Sunday. They have been playing poorly recently because their striker, Papiss Cisse, is banned.

Newcastle is currently at the bottom of the Premier League, just one point above the teams that will be relegated. However, if it weren’t for Cisse’s goals, Sunderland would actually be two points lower than Newcastle in the relegation zone.

Cisse is Newcastle’s best scorer this season with 11 goals. Ten of those goals were crucial in helping Newcastle win games.

Dick Advocaat is bringing Lee Cattermole back to the center of his Sunderland team. Cattermole is 27 years old and known for being tough on the field. He missed the last two games because he was suspended after receiving 10 yellow cards this season. Because of this suspension, he could not play in Advocaat’s first game as manager, which was a 1-0 loss to West Ham on March 21.

Now, Advocaat wants to win another derby match against Newcastle. This would be his fifth straight victory in these games. At a team meeting on Friday, Cattermole was the only player told he would definitely start the game on Sunday. Advocaat is hoping for a strong performance from Cattermole

For Ronny Deila, qualifying for the Champions League isn’t just about money. However, there is a strong financial reason for him to lead Celtic to win their fourth straight title: £16 million. This week, UEFA announced the payment schedule for European competitions over the next three years. When Celtic last reached the Champions League group stage in 2013–14, playing against AC Milan, Ajax, and Barcelona, they won one game and earned £12.6 million. If they achieve the same result (or better) next season, they would earn £4 million more. If they advance to the round of 16, their earnings would exceed £20 million. This amount does not even include money from ticket sales.

Tottenham defender Ben Davies will not let personal feelings get in the way when he plays against his Wales teammate, Sam Vokes, at Burnley on Sunday.

Tottenham is going to Turf Moor hoping to keep up their good form. They have won three of their last four Premier League games, with only one loss to Manchester United before the break for international matches. They are trying to stay in the race for a spot in European competitions.

Burnley is fighting to avoid being relegated. They are currently in 18th place, but only one point away from safety.

Earlier this season, in the FA Cup, Sam Vokes scored for Burnley against Tottenham. Ben Davies looked upset after Burnley tied the game in that match.

Neil Redfearn is thinking about whether to stay on as manager of Leeds United. This comes after the club suspended his assistant, Steve Thompson, on Thursday.

It took the club two months to hire Thompson, but he was fired after only 105 days. On Wednesday morning, Nicola Salerno, the director of football, sent Thompson a letter saying he is suspended until the end of the season. This means Thompson will not stay at the club (Elland Road) for the rest of the year.

Thompson was told he will remain suspended until his contract ends at the end of the season. The club also told him that they will not renew his contract.

John Carver says he will push his Newcastle players hard to make sure they are motivated for Sunday’s big game against Sunderland at the Stadium of Light. Newcastle has lost the last four matches against their local rivals. Carver, who was Alan Pardew’s assistant during those losses, admits that Sunderland wanted to win more than Newcastle did. He said, “In the last four games, Sunderland worked harder than us—and that’s not a good thing.” Carver says he will “whip” his players to ensure they are ready to beat Sunderland on Sunday.

David Templeton criticized the training methods used by former Rangers managers Ally McCoist and Kenny McDowall. He said that new coach Stuart McCall has introduced better coaching and tactics, which were missing before. Templeton praised McCall, who took over on a short-term deal last month, for his positive impact. Back-to-back wins have boosted the team's confidence ahead of Saturday's home game against Hearts, who are leading the Championship.

Nolito, a forward for Celta Vigo, says Lionel Messi should stay home and enjoy the beach on Sunday instead of playing in their La Liga match. Messi has been training after having a minor foot problem and is expected to be ready for the game. However, the 28-year-old Nolito told the newspaper Marca that he prefers Messi not to play. He joked that he would call Messi’s father to suggest he stay away. Despite the injury, Messi is expected to be fit to play against Celta Vigo. On Thursday, Messi was seen training with his teammate Javier Mascherano.

Hearts manager Robbie Neilson says he will only let players like captain Danny Wilson leave if it is good for the club. Sportsmail reported this week that Celtic wants to sign Wilson in the summer. Neilson admitted that other clubs showing interest in his young players is normal. He says he will not sell any players unless it is the right decision for Hearts. Like the club’s owner, Ann Budge, Neilson says he alone decides if a player can leave, and only if the price is right.

Sam Allardyce, the manager of West Ham, has warned Brendan Rodgers that giving Raheem Sterling a very large new contract might cause problems for the rest of the Liverpool team. Allardyce believes that if Sterling is paid more than the £100,000 per week he was previously offered, his teammates will ask for higher salaries too.

However, Allardyce does not blame Sterling for trying to get the best possible deal. Sterling currently earns £35,000 a week at Liverpool. Allardyce thinks that because there are so few talented young players available, clubs are willing to pay huge amounts of money to sign any good young talent they can find.
